frameworks.name: Best-fit customer research: who to learn from and by which method
frameworks.decision: Whom to recruit for research and whether to run interviews, a survey, or both
evidence_required: List of paying customers with start date
A value-realized signal per customer (usage, renewals, repeat orders, owner judgement)
Consent basis to contact customers for research
prerequisites: At least some customers who have solved their problem with the product
A named decision the research must inform (Book 02 §1)

branches.if: Decision is what to say, whom to target or which Job to serve (attract more of the best)
branches.then: Recruit best-fit customers per BK08-F6 (recent payers who reached value).

branches.if: Decision is why people fail to activate, stall or churn
branches.then: Recruit for contrast (Book 02 §5): stalled evaluators, churned and non-buyers, kept as separate pools; best-fit customers only as a comparison pool.

branches.if: Best-fit pool is large (author heuristic: 500+)
branches.then: Start with a short open-ended survey; target 25-50 good answers; follow with interviews.

branches.if: Best-fit pool is small, or time for only one method
branches.then: 10-15 interviews (or PB-interviews saturation stop).

branches.if: No best-fit customers yet
branches.then: Go to BK08-K2 audience research; label results as hypotheses.

steps: State the decision
Filter customers: felt the problem, pay without hesitation, ongoing need, value realized, started 3-6 months ago (up to 12)
Count the pool and choose method
Ask what happened in sequence (old way, trigger, search, choice, certainty moment, new capability)
Keep raw answers with respondent counts
exceptions_failure_modes: Only happy customers interviewed for a churn question (selection bias)
Long-tenured customers cannot recall the trigger
Survey sent under marketing-only consent
Owner 'is the customer' and skips research (BK08-F10)

requirements.labor: Owner 5-10 hours for 10-15 interviews; less for a survey
requirements.capability: Contact list, survey form or calendar
requirements.measurement: Respondent and invite counts; response rate

metrics: Share of answers that describe events rather than opinions
guardrails: No synthetic respondents or invented quotes
Owner approves every send; sends only from owner's channels with a consent basis
stop_review: Survey under 10 usable answers after 14 days: switch to interviews (CH-C2)
Interviews stop adding new struggle themes: stop
Answers scattered across many Jobs after ~10: narrow the segment (PB-interviews revise)
alternatives: No list or consent: audience research (BK08-K2) or public review mining (voc-research)
Tiny pool (<10 best customers): 3-5 interviews plus competitor reviews, labelled thin
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The book's selection rule optimises for 'more of the customers we want'. It is the right sample for positioning and acquisition messaging and the wrong sample for diagnosing a leak, which Book 02 and BK05 handle by recruiting for contrast.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: PB-interviews v2 chooses the recruitment pool from the decision: best-fit recent payers for targeting/messaging decisions; contrast pools (stalled, churned, non-buyers) for activation/conversion/retention diagnoses.
proposed: the 500-customer survey threshold and 10-15% response rate are shown as author heuristics, never as expected yields; the plan uses the owner's own list size and states the assumed rate.
proposed: participants should have started paying within about 12 months so they can recall the trigger; older customers go in a separate pool.
proposed: no research send without a recorded consent basis and owner approval.

relation_to_existing.note: PB-interviews has no participant-selection rule and no survey branch; CH-C2 adds surveys but not best-fit selection. Candidate PB-interviews v2.

frameworks.disagreements: Book 02 §5 says recruit for contrast, not applause; FTF says learn only from the best. What decides: the decision type. Messaging/targeting decisions favour best-fit; leak diagnosis needs contrast. BK05/guide 05 favour episode questions about any recent instance; FTF's script is a success-story reconstruction. Both agree on past events over opinions.

frameworks.name: Future-customer research: website visitor survey and audience research
frameworks.decision: What message to lead with and what blocks signup when own-customer evidence is thin or the target is new
evidence_required: Public sources where the audience talks (for audience research)
prerequisites: Owner permission to add an on-site survey

branches.if: Site has steady traffic
branches.then: Run a short on-site survey: awareness stage (closed), current tool, dislikes, what matters most, what holds them back (open).

branches.if: Low or no traffic, or new market
branches.then: Audience research via voc-research (reviews, forums), target-market interviews, subscriber survey.

branches.if: Best-fit customers exist too
branches.then: Use own-customer research (K1) first; visitor survey adds message order and blockers.

steps: Write the decision and the five question slots in own words
Estimate days to reach the response target from the owner's traffic and an assumed response rate
Launch with owner approval; keep it running in background
Code answers: awareness mix, current alternative, dislikes, priority, blockers
Rank 'what matters most' themes to set homepage order; blockers go near the CTA (CH-C5)
exceptions_failure_modes: Treating respondents as ideal customers
Survey placed on the conversion step and hurting signups
Existing customers logging in counted as prospects

requirements.cash: Survey tool may cost; ClimbOS should build its own snippet first (build-own rule)
requirements.capability: Ability to add a script to the site
requirements.measurement: Impressions, responses, signup rate before/after on comparable traffic

metrics: Share of 'already a customer' answers (screen out)
Signup rate of surveyed vs not-surveyed sessions
guardrails: Answers labelled 'prospect, fit unknown' and never pooled with own-customer evidence
No personal data required to answer
Do not place on checkout or signup form
stop_review: Signup rate on survey pages drops vs prior period: move or remove survey
Projected time to target exceeds ~8 weeks: switch to audience research
alternatives: No site edit access: ask 5 recent inquirers the same questions by reply
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The visitor survey is a cheap, consent-light source of prospect language and blockers; ClimbOS currently has none. Its evidence is weaker than best-customer data and should carry a lower confidence label.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: voc-research gets a 'site visitor' pool with its own N, confidence ceiling Medium, never blended with own-customer or competitor pools.
proposed: before recommending a visitor survey, compute days-to-target from owner traffic and an explicit assumed rate in code; if over 8 weeks, offer audience research instead.
proposed: installing a survey on the owner's site is an external action requiring owner approval.

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/voc-research/SKILL.md (new source branch); skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md (message order, blockers near CTA)

relation_to_existing.note: CH-C2 covers buyer surveys and a post-purchase poll; no repo file covers a pre-purchase on-site visitor survey (repo search found none).

frameworks.disagreements: Book 02 §4 warns a survey characterises its sampling frame only; FTF agrees in substance (results are hypotheses). Copyhackers ranks by theme frequency; FTF orders by 'what matters most'. Both decide order from counted answers, so no conflict.

frameworks.name: Job statements from coded research, then pick one Job
frameworks.decision: Which customer Job to build messaging, channels and onboarding around first
evidence_required: Coded research answers (K1/K2) with respondent IDs
Per-Job signals for urgency, willingness to pay, support burden, retention, expansion, reachability
prerequisites: At least ~10 coded respondents, or labelled thin

branches.if: One struggle theme dominates and scores well on the criteria
branches.then: Choose it; park others.

branches.if: Most frequent Job scores worse on payment, retention or reachability than another
branches.then: Present both; criteria and owner strategy decide, frequency is one input.

branches.if: Respondents mix segments with different buying processes
branches.then: Code segments separately before counting (guide 05).

branches.if: Fewer than 3 respondents share a struggle
branches.then: Signal only; do not write a Job statement on it.

steps: Tag every answer with struggle, motivation and desired-outcome themes, one dimension at a time
Count struggle themes as n of N respondents
For each top struggle, filter to its respondents and count their motivations and outcomes
Write 2-3 'when / help me / so I can' statements in customer words
Score each Job on the selection criteria with evidence notes; unknowns stay unknown
Pick one; log the runner-up and why
exceptions_failure_modes: Trying to serve all Jobs at once (book's top mistake)
Counts read as market share
Job statements paraphrased into company jargon
Ignoring anxieties and habits that block switching

requirements.labor: 2-4 hours of coding for 15-50 answers (model-assisted, owner-checked)

metrics: Conditional share of motivation within a struggle
After choosing: signup and first-value rates for the chosen Job's traffic
guardrails: Every theme count shows n of N and pool
Criteria scores cite evidence or say unknown
stop_review: Chosen Job's messaging shows no change in signup or first-value rate after the planned window: revisit choice or execution
New research shows the Job's trigger changed: redo
alternatives: No research: owner's notes from 5 best clients coded the same way, labelled owner-reported
Very small sample: keep Jobs as hypotheses and test messages per Job in ads or email
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: FTF's struggle/motivation/outcome coding overlaps voc-research's push/pull/outcome tags, but adds two missing steps: the conditional cross-tab (motivations within a struggle) and an explicit one-Job choice. The choice criteria resemble Book 02 §8's importance profile and the channel-scoring factors.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: voc-research outputs 2-3 Job statements built from the conditional cross-tab, each with n of N, and a one-Job recommendation with the runner-up.
proposed: theme percentages and conditional shares are computed in code from coded rows, never written by the model.
proposed: a Job statement needs a struggle theme seen in at least 3 respondents from the same pool (matches voc-research 'finding' bar).
proposed: when the most frequent Job is not the best on payment, retention or reachability, show both and let the owner choose.

relation_to_existing.note: No repo file contains job statements or a one-Job selection step (search for 'job statement' found none).

frameworks.disagreements: voc-research codes four forces including anxiety and habit; FTF's statement drops them. Keep four-force coding and add the statement; anxieties feed objections. Book 02 §7 warns counts do not estimate prevalence; FTF uses counts to rank. Both hold if counts rank within the sample and are not reported as market share.

frameworks.name: Customer-experience map: phases and milestones vs ClimbOS's funnel stages
frameworks.decision: Which stages to measure for this business and where the purchase sits in them
evidence_required: Which events the owner can observe
prerequisites: Some way to observe at least one value event

branches.if: Recurring or repeat revenue
branches.then: Map all three phases; Growth (continued value, value growth) is measured, not optional.

branches.if: One-off purchase (emergency repair, single high-ticket job)
branches.then: A purchase funnel plus a review/referral step is adequate; Growth phase reduces to referral and rebooking.

branches.if: Owner only has counts of visitors, leads and customers
branches.then: Diagnose with diagnosis.ts stages, define activation as value received, and make instrumenting one value milestone the first step.

branches.if: Enterprise buyer
branches.then: Expect more Evaluation milestones (stakeholders, security, onboarding many users).

steps: Lay out Struggle, Evaluation, Growth
Place evidence under thinking, doing, feeling per phase
Split into milestones where feelings shift
Map each milestone to a diagnosis.ts stage (Problem→reach, Interest→lead, First Value→activation, Value Realization→activation(value)/purchase, Continued Value→retention, Value Growth→no stage today)
Note where payment happens for this business
exceptions_failure_modes: Generic awareness/consideration/purchase stages pasted in
Milestones invented without customer evidence
Map made for all Jobs at once

requirements.labor: A half-day workshop equivalent; ClimbOS drafts from research
requirements.measurement: At least one value event per phase eventually

metrics: Milestones with an observable KPI / total milestones
guardrails: Stages with no data marked unmeasured, not guessed
stop_review: Research for the Job is older than ~12 months or the product changed: refresh
alternatives: No research: draft milestones from owner interview, labelled owner-reported
No event data: owner hand-marks a sample of recent customers per milestone
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: The book's 'forget the funnel' is a critique of generic stage names, purchase-as-endpoint and business-value metrics. It does not reject sequential stage-to-stage ratios: Ch8 picks the gap where many reach one milestone and few reach the next, which is funnel arithmetic on customer-value milestones. ClimbOS's diagnosis already moved toward this (activation as value received, diagnosis.ts:17-23) but has no expansion stage.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: for recurring-revenue types, the diagnosis reports a retention reading and, when supplied, an expansion reading (upgrades, added seats, referrals); missing Growth-phase numbers are listed in 'missing'.
proposed: stage labels shown to the owner use the business's own milestone names where defined, while code keeps the fixed stage keys.
proposed: one-off purchase businesses keep the purchase funnel; ClimbOS does not force a Growth-phase map on them.

relation_to_existing.note: Book 08 §2 already defines lifecycle states around customer progress (prospect...expanding). FTF adds the evidence-based method (thinking/doing/feeling, feeling shifts) and a per-Job map.

frameworks.disagreements: Tension with the title: ClimbOS diagnoses a funnel. What decides: (1) revenue model: recurring or repeat revenue needs Growth-phase stages; one-off sales can live with a purchase funnel; (2) data: ClimbOS can only diagnose what the owner can count, so a funnel of counts is the floor, defined by value events; (3) decision: choosing which stage to work on needs sequential ratios under either framing. Disagree with FTF that generic stages are useless: fixed stage keys let code compare and lint plays; customer-specific milestone names can sit on top.

frameworks.name: Customer-led KPI per milestone
frameworks.decision: Which metric represents each stage and which metrics team or plan targets use
evidence_required: Customer statements of value mapped to features or service elements
Event or job data per customer
Later paid/retained outcome per customer for validation

branches.if: Product runs in the background (automation, scheduled sends)
branches.then: Value KPI is the outcome event (sent, delivered, error-free), never logins.

branches.if: Enough cohort volume to compare later payment
branches.then: Validate thresholds: users reaching the KPI must pay or retain clearly more than those who do not (BRP-07 step 5).

branches.if: Too few users to validate
branches.then: Keep threshold as a labelled hypothesis; owner marks 10-20 recent signups.

branches.if: Top-of-journey metric
branches.then: Use new unique visitors, excluding logins and returning customers.

steps: List what customers said was valuable per milestone
Map each to the feature or service element that delivers it
Write a trackable action (with threshold if data supports) per milestone
Continued Value = value KPI within a period matched to natural use frequency
Value Growth = continued value plus upgrade, review or referral
Validate against later outcomes; adjust
Dashboard and benchmark before choosing work
exceptions_failure_modes: DAU/MAU or logins as engagement
Shared metric across teams causing misattribution
Thresholds copied from the book's SparkToro example
Lagging metrics (MRR) used as stage targets

requirements.labor: Setup of events or manual counts

metrics: Rate reaching each milestone KPI within window
Paid/retained rate conditional on reaching vs not
guardrails: Rates computed in code with denominators
Pair any milestone lift with downstream paid or retained outcome
stop_review: KPI reachers do not pay/retain better than non-reachers: move the definition
Nearly everyone reaches it: it is setup, move later
alternatives: No tracking: weekly owner count from admin view
Service business: milestone = job delivered, problem gone, rebooked
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: For activation this duplicates BRP-07 (Verna), which is stricter because it validates the definition against later payment. New from FTF: the full ladder (problem, interest, continued value per period, value growth), new-unique-visitor counting, and the metric-incentive warning.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: BRP-07 v2 extends the value-event definition to every milestone, including Continued Value (value KPI per natural period) and Value Growth (plus upgrade, review or referral).
proposed: a milestone threshold is 'validated' only when reachers' later paid or retained rate exceeds non-reachers' in the same cohort; otherwise label 'hypothesis'.
proposed: the owner's 'visitors' input asks for new unique visitors and excludes logged-in customers.
proposed: NPS/CSAT may be reported but never used as a milestone KPI or a diagnosis input.

relation_to_existing.note: Activation part duplicates BRP-07; candidate BRP-07 v2 for the full ladder.

frameworks.disagreements: FTF lists signups and NPS/CSAT as leading indicators while warning against transactional and opinion measures; ClimbOS should keep signups as a lead-stage count and keep NPS out of diagnosis. FTF sets thresholds by judgment; Verna (BRP-07) requires validation. What decides: cohort volume. With enough signups, validate; without, label hypothesis.

frameworks.name: Success-gap selection and bridging
frameworks.decision: Which stage-to-stage gap to fix first and which few projects to run on it
evidence_required: Counts reaching each milestone in a period

branches.if: Many reach a milestone and few reach the next
branches.then: Candidate gap; size it by added customers per realistic lift times value.

branches.if: Two gaps are close
branches.then: Prefer the one actionable in weeks with existing people and tools.

branches.if: Walk-through finds a gap but counts do not show a drop
branches.then: Treat as a hypothesis or service-quality fix, not the binding constraint.

branches.if: Diagnosis constraint is delivery (capacity)
branches.then: Do not add demand-side projects; capacity overrides (diagnosis.ts:130).

steps: Walk each milestone as the chosen-Job customer: their search places, ads, homepage, signup, first use, emails, renewal
List mismatches per milestone
Read stage counts and rates (code)
Size each candidate gap deterministically
Pick one; park others
Shortlist 2-4 projects deliverable in weeks
Measure with the milestone KPI and downstream paid/retained; schedule a recurring check
exceptions_failure_modes: Picking the most fun or trendy idea
Fixing several gaps at once and learning nothing
Treating a walk-through mismatch as the proven cause
Feeding traffic into a leaking activation stage

requirements.cash: Usually none to low (copy, onboarding, emails)
requirements.labor: Owner time for walk-through and fixes
requirements.capability: Ability to edit site, onboarding or emails
requirements.measurement: Whole-week cohorts before/after or a split when volume allows

metrics: Milestone KPI rate for new cohorts
guardrails: Lift claims carry window, cohort and comparison
Book case uplifts never used as forecasts
Customer-facing sends follow consent rules (lifecycle email only to consented contacts; Resend never for cold)
stop_review: No change after planned weeks: gap cause was elsewhere
Milestone up, paid flat: look at offer or price (PB-activation-repair revise)
alternatives: No counts: owner hand-checks last 20 signups through each milestone
Low volume: before/after on whole weeks, labelled directional
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: This is the same job diagnosis.ts does (weakest link) plus a customer walk-through to generate repair ideas. FTF weighs absolute revenue effect; diagnosis.ts compares activation and purchase rates directly (diagnosis.ts:134). Book 08 §3's expected-contribution formula is the deterministic version of FTF's 'outsized impact' test.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: when two measured gaps compete, code reports added customers and contribution for the same point lift at each stage (eligible x lift x downstream rate x value) next to the rate comparison.
proposed: plans include a 'walk the journey' first step that lists mismatches per milestone, labelled as hypotheses.
proposed: book case uplifts (2x, +93%, +64%) appear only as labelled historical examples, never as expected results.

frameworks.climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts diagnose(), lintDiagnosisFit; PB-activation-repair; skills/growth-strategy/SKILL.md; skills/retention-lifecycle/SKILL.md step 3

relation_to_existing.note: Gap choice duplicates the existing weakest-link logic; new parts are the walk-through audit, the per-milestone project menu and volume-weighted sizing.

frameworks.disagreements: FTF implies the walk-through reveals what to fix; Book 08 §17 warns counts describe but do not diagnose, and a cause needs verified evidence. Both hold: the walk-through generates hypotheses, counts locate the gap, a test confirms. diagnosis.ts uses lowest rate; FTF uses largest revenue effect. What decides: when volumes differ a lot between stages, sizing in absolute customers is more informative; keep the rate rule as the default and show sizing as explanation.

frameworks.name: Customer-led operating cadence (one Job, map-tagged plans, refresh triggers)
frameworks.decision: How plans stay tied to the chosen Job and when to redo research

branches.if: Solo owner
branches.then: ClimbOS acts as facilitator; owner is decision-maker and champion; skip team roles.

branches.if: Team of 5+
branches.then: Name a champion and an accountable decision-maker; share the map.

branches.if: Product, pricing, segment or market changed, or research older than ~12 months
branches.then: Refresh research for the Job.

branches.if: First Job's gap bridged and stable
branches.then: Return to a tabled Job or a new segment.

steps: Every play states the Job, milestone and KPI it moves
Review KPI dashboard on a fixed cadence
Log which gap is being worked and which are parked
Trigger research refresh on change events
exceptions_failure_modes: Map shelved after the workshop
Plays not tied to any milestone
Research never refreshed
metrics: Share of plays tagged to the chosen Job's milestone
guardrails: Tags are checked by code, not trusted from prose
stop_review: Over half the plays target other milestones than the chosen gap: re-focus or justify
alternatives: No dashboard: monthly manual counts per milestone
frameworks.interpretation: INTERPRETATION: ClimbOS already enforces a version of this (plays must work on the computed constraint, diagnosis.ts:171-175). FTF adds tagging by Job and refresh triggers. The team-role chapter mostly does not apply to solo owners.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: each play carries a milestone tag and the chosen Job id; lint flags plans where the bankable play is not on the chosen gap.
proposed: research older than 12 months or predating a pricing/product change is shown as stale.

relation_to_existing.note: Constraint-fit lint exists; Job tagging and research staleness do not.

frameworks.disagreements: FTF's cross-functional team setup assumes 6-200 staff; ClimbOS's owners are often solo. What decides: team size.

skill_proposals.change: Add an own-customer branch: select best-fit recent payers (or contrast pools when the decision is a leak), choose survey vs interviews from pool size with the rate stated as an assumption, and keep a separate 'site visitor' pool for an on-site survey. After four-force coding, add a step that cross-tabs motivations and outcomes within each top struggle, writes 2-3 'when / help me / so I can' statements with n of N, and recommends one Job with a runner-up scored on urgency, willingness to pay, support burden, retention, expansion and reachability.
skill_proposals.why: Skill covers public reviews only and stops at insights; no job statement or one-Job choice exists in the repo.

skill_proposals.change: In step 6 (best-fit customers), take the chosen Job's struggle as the trigger event and its desired outcome as the value theme; disqualify the other Jobs' buyers explicitly for now.
skill_proposals.why: Links Dunford's best-fit segment to FTF's one-Job focus without duplicating it.

skill_proposals.change: In step 2, define Continued Value as the value moment repeated within the natural use period and Value Growth as upgrade, added seats, review or referral; warn against login-based engagement for background products.
skill_proposals.why: Step 2 defines the value moment and repeat cycle but not the growth-phase milestones.

skill_proposals.change: When the product has many features, lead with the one gateway outcome customers hired it for and move others to later onboarding messages; order sections by the visitor survey's 'what matters most' ranking when available.
skill_proposals.why: Autobooks and Alistair cases; complements CH-C1 theme-rank ordering.

skill_proposals.change: Add a journey walk-through step: as the chosen-Job customer, check each milestone (search places, ads, homepage, signup, first use, emails, renewal), list mismatches as hypotheses, then size the measured gaps in code and pick one.
skill_proposals.why: Generates repair ideas tied to the computed constraint.

code_gaps.gap: StageReading.stage has no expansion/value-growth stage and OwnerFunnel (11-26) has no expansion input, so recurring businesses get no reading for upgrades, added seats or referrals.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add optional `expanded` count to OwnerFunnel and an 'expansion' reading with verdict 'unknown' (no benchmark in base-rates.md); list it in `missing` for SaaS types. Do not add a constraint until there is a reference.

code_gaps.gap: playStage maps 'upgrade' to conversion, so an existing-customer upsell or annual-switch play can satisfy lintDiagnosisFit (171-175) when the constraint is first-purchase conversion.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Distinguish trial/free-to-paid upgrade from existing-customer upgrade (tier, seats, annual) and map the latter to retention/expansion.

code_gaps.gap: `visitors` is 'people who saw the offer'; owners may enter total sessions including logged-in customers, inflating the reach denominator and the demand test at line 137 (perMonth(visitors) < 1000).
code_gaps.proposed_change: Reword the input to 'new unique visitors (not logged-in customers)' and in the owner UI ask whether the figure includes logins.

code_gaps.gap: Funnel has no segment or Job dimension; mixed Jobs are aggregated, so one Job's leak can be masked by another's success.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Optional segment label with per-segment counts; diagnose the chosen Job's segment when supplied (pairs with BRP-10 signup profiling).

code_gaps.gap: Activation vs conversion is chosen by lower rate only; absolute effect (eligible volume x lift x downstream rate x value) is not shown.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add a deterministic sizing line to diagnosisBrief for the two candidate stages using a fixed point lift; keep the rate rule for the choice.

code_gaps.gap: PB-interviews has no participant-selection rule (best-fit recent payers vs contrast pools) and no survey branch for large customer pools.
code_gaps.proposed_change: PB-interviews v2: recruitment pool chosen by decision type; survey branch when the owner's filtered pool is large; recency rule (started within ~12 months).

code_gaps.gap: Inputs and sources are public reviews and forums only; no own-customer survey or on-site visitor survey branch.
code_gaps.proposed_change: See skill_proposals; add pools 'own-customer survey' and 'site visitor' with separate N and confidence ceilings.
